classification.difficultyReason: Requires sign cases for two absolute-value expressions and reconciliation of the resulting intervals.

answer.worked:
For $x\le-1$,
$$\begin{align*}|x|-|x+1|&=-x+(x+1)\\|x|-|x+1|&=1.\end{align*}$$
Every $x\le-1$ satisfies the inequality.

For $-1<x<0$,
$$\begin{align*}|x|-|x+1|&=-x-(x+1)\\|x|-|x+1|&=-2x-1.\end{align*}$$
Thus
$$\begin{align*}-2x-1&\ge\frac12\\-2x&\ge\frac32\\x&\le-\frac34.\end{align*}$$
Within this case, $-1<x\le-\frac34$.

For $x\ge0$, $|x|-|x+1|=-1$, so there are no solutions in this case.

Combining the intervals gives $x\le-\frac34$.
